title: Protection of Egyptian Antiquities and Cultural Heritage Export Laws
perspective: Egyptian Heritage Sovereignty & National Antiquities Protection
summary: Egypt takes immense pride in its multi-millennial civilization. The Egyptian state enforces strict laws to protect its heritage against smuggling, illegal excavation, or unauthorized export.

sections.heading: Antiquities Protection Law (Law No. 117 of 1983 & Amendments)
content: State Ownership of Heritage: All Egyptian antiquities—whether pharaonic, Coptic, Islamic, or modern historical—are the exclusive national property of the State of Egypt.

Strict Export Prohibition: It is strictly illegal to export, sell, possess, or transport any authentic antique, artifact, or historical relic without an explicit permit from the Supreme Council of Antiquities.

Severe Legal Penalties: Antiquities smuggling and illegal excavation carry maximum penalties under Egyptian law, including life imprisonment with hard labor and hefty fines running into millions of Egyptian pounds.

Purchasing Replica Souvenirs: Tourists and visitors are encouraged to purchase official high-quality replicas manufactured by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities (e.g., Konouz Egypt Replica Factory). When purchasing high-end replicas, buyers should keep official sales receipts to show customs officers upon departure.
